title: Run dataset (0.3.0)
description: A run's data, derived deterministically from its log, joined and flattened into examples a training run can use (docs/design/run-datasets.md). A folder per run: manifest.json (Manifest), systems.jsonl (SystemPrompt), translations.jsonl (Translation), decisions.jsonl (Decision), and optionally actions.jsonl (Action), observations.jsonl (ObservationRow), citizen_decisions.jsonl (CitizenDecision) and citizen_outcomes.jsonl (CitizenOutcome). The log stays the record; a dataset can always be made again from it.

log.description: The log it was made from: its file name, entries, and the last entry's hash (which pins the whole chain).

versions.description: What made the run: contracts, kernel, orchestrator, behaviour modules (name -> {version, sha256}), translator.

seats.description: The language-model seats: participant -> the model configured and the one used; and the price table.

files.description: Each file written: its rows, and how many are synthetic (from the mock).

citizens.description: What the run recorded for citizen models (docs/design/ai-citizens.md 7): decisions and outcomes in all, and by area of life how many decisions were recorded, how many of them the citizen learned at least one outcome of, and how many outcomes (those following no recorded decision included). Absent: the log holds no citizen's decision.

Turn.description: One model call in an exchange: what it was shown (the last message) and what it answered, in full.

Executed.description: A command carried out: its place in the log, and whether the kernel applied it (and if not, why).

Command.description: A command a participant gave, as logged, and what came of it.

applied.description: For an act: whether it was applied, or refused (`refusal`: why), joined by the act's action (an act takes time, and how it ended is logged when it ends). Absent: not an act, or still under way when the log ended.

created.description: The ids of what the act made, as the log's events for it say: records (a notice, a decision, an order, an agreement) and letters. What is later written in answer names one of them.

Decision.description: A language-model participant's model call: what it was shown, what it answered, what followed in the world, and what had come back of its earlier acts.

came_back.description: What the seat had been shown, since its last model call, that names something an earlier act of its own made: a reply to its letter, a decision on its form, a paper made on its direction, a vote on its proposal. `of`: the id of what the seat made; `seq`: the command that made it (a row of some earlier call's `commands`); `in`: the id of the record or letter that names it (in observations.jsonl); `from`: who wrote it, for a letter. A join by reference and nothing more: it does not say whether what came back was what the seat wanted.

Action.description: An act by a code participant: the rule it followed (in words), the call, the blocks, and whether it was applied.

applied.description: Whether the act was applied, or refused (`refusal`: why). Joined by the act's action: an act takes time, and how it ended is logged when it ends. Absent: still under way when the log ended.

created.description: The ids of what the act made, as the log's events for it say: records (a notice, a decision, an order, an agreement) and letters. What is later written in answer names one of them.

ObservationRow.description: An observation a participant received (recorded only when the run was asked to): what's new since its last.

CitizenDecision.description: A code citizen's decision, as its mind made it (docs/design/ai-citizens.md 7): what it had before it (each option's facts, how many it knows took it, what it means to them, what they have learned of it; their routine; their circumstances), how it decided (repeat, imitate, compare, deliberate), each option's score (basis points), what it chose, and what the citizen then came to know of how the choice turned out (`outcomes`). Facts as the citizen had them, and the mind's own figures: nothing here says whether a choice was good. Training data for citizen models, and the baseline they're compared with. What the citizen did next is in the log after `seq`, by the same participant (actions.jsonl rows carry `seq`).

seq.description: Where the decision stands in the run's log (the annotation's sequence number): the citizen's acts that carried it out, and what came of them, are that participant's entries after it.

n.description: The citizen's own count of its recorded decisions, from 1 (it starts again if the citizen's controller does): what an outcome names as the decision it follows.

follows.description: The earlier decision of the citizen's (its `n`) that this one follows up: trying another shop for what the trip's shop could not serve.

facts.description: What taking it up would change in a month, as the citizen appraised it (from an offer's typed terms): money in (+) or out (-), in minor units; a home, and its bedrooms where known; hours of work; goods (units); company (people); hours of one's own time.

others.description: How many people the citizen knows took it (told so, or led there).

meaning.description: What it means to them beyond its facts, from what they believe or were told (basis points; may be negative).

learned.description: What the citizen has learned of it from their own experience and what others told them (its attraction, on the payoff scale: basis points), when it decided. Absent: never tried nor heard of.

options.description: Every option the citizen had before it, by key. `score` is 0 where the way of deciding gave it none: all of them under repeat; under imitate, those nobody known to the citizen took.

current.description: The option that is the citizen's routine, if they have one.

circumstances.description: Where the citizen stood: the household's income a month and their savings (minor units), whether without a home, the bedrooms the household needs (home decisions), and what a month's essentials cost in their world.

satisfied_here.description: How this area of life has gone for them, where the decision was given it (basis points).

doubt.description: What a feeling (fear) took from how sure they were of their options (basis points), when above 0.

person.description: Who the citizen is: values, temperament and how much each need weighs (basis points; weights 10000 to 20000). It does not change, and comes with a citizen's first recorded decision only (again after a restart of its controller).

state.description: The citizen's state behind the decision (docs/design/contracts-0.7.md A2): the core (needs, satisfaction, certainty) always; emotion, beliefs and goal when there are any. Versioned by the mind that produced it.

outcomes.description: What the citizen came to know of how this choice turned out, in the order it learned it: each time it was served, paid or not, each gathering gone to, and how it ended (the job, the tenancy). Each is an outcome of the citizen's latest decision that chose the option. Present wherever the run recorded outcomes. Empty: the citizen learned nothing of it before the run ended (manifest `end.t`): it is not known, which is not a payoff of nought. Absent: the log was made before outcomes were recorded.

t.description: When the citizen came to know it (not when it happened: a wage is known when the citizen next looks at its account).

seq.description: Where the record stands in the run's log (the annotation's sequence number; one annotation holds all a citizen learned since its last action).

option.description: What it is about, as the citizen's decisions name their options: the shop, the employer, the home (its space), the gathering, `stay`, `member`, a goal and its method.

kind.description: What happened, in a word. shop: served. job: hired, paid, unpaid, rise, ended. home: lease_signed, moved_in, not_in_yet, rent_increase, renewed, notice_received, ended. practice: attended, turned_away, stayed, expected. membership: joined, rise_won, stoppage_called. goal: met, not_met. venture: founded, refused, capital_called. petition: signatures, closed. Any area: told (another's experience, as they told it). belief: told. A reader should take a kind it does not know as a fact of that name.

way.description: How the citizen came to know (docs/design/knowing.md): mine (its own money, papers and letters, and what its own acts came to), here (it was there), published, ask.

facts.description: What happened, as the citizen has it: counts, sums in minor units, days, ids, yes or no. By kind: served: ordered, delivered, refund, order. paid: amount, agreed, paid_at, days_since_last, period_days. unpaid: days_since_last, period_days, periods_missed, owed. hired: wage, period_days, days_without, after_notice. ended: by (self, other, term), held_days, rent, unpaid. rise: rise_bps, wage, made_at. lease_signed: rent, days_without. rent_increase: rent, was, from, bearable, challenged. renewed: rent, was. not_in_yet: why. attended: host, others, meaning. met, not_met: level, wanted, days. told: served_bps, paid, goes, host. Nothing here is a judgement.

learned.description: The mind's update of what it has learned of the option (experience-weighted attraction; basis points on the payoff scale): the payoff the mind computed from what happened, and the option's attraction before and after. `first`: never tried nor heard of before, so `before` is what the citizen expected of it. `heard`: another's payoff, weighed as such (below one's own experience). An update also fades what the citizen has learned of the area's other options; the next decision's options carry them.

need.description: The need the mind read the payoff from, or that the outcome is a level of (an evening at home is worth the company one has there: social; a goal is met when its need recovers).

felt.description: Feelings the mind appraised from it: the emotion, about whom, the strength of the cause (basis points), and the feeling's level before and after.

belief.description: How strongly the citizen holds what `host` teaches (the strongest of its teachings; basis points), before and after.

CitizenOutcome.description: One thing a code citizen came to know of how something went, when and as it came to know it (docs/design/ai-citizens.md 7): the flat list of what is nested under decisions in citizen_decisions.jsonl, with what follows no recorded decision (a job or home held from the start; what someone told them of a shop, an employer or a gathering; what they expected of something before trying it). Facts as the citizen had them and the mind's own figures. Nothing here says whether an outcome was good, and nothing is here that the citizen did not know.

t.description: When the citizen came to know it (not when it happened: a wage is known when the citizen next looks at its account).

seq.description: Where the record stands in the run's log (the annotation's sequence number; one annotation holds all a citizen learned since its last action).

domain.description: The area of life, as decisions name it (shop, job, home, practice, membership, goal, venture, petition); `belief` for what the citizen holds.

option.description: What it is about, as the citizen's decisions name their options: the shop, the employer, the home (its space), the gathering, `stay`, `member`, a goal and its method.

of.description: The decision it follows from: that decision's `n` (the citizen's latest that chose this option). Absent: no recorded decision began it.

decision_t.description: When that decision was made: `t` less this is how long the citizen waited to know.
